newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's mining firm seeks Busang involvement.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's mining firm seeks Busang involvement.

text.p: Indonesia's state owned gold and nickel mining company PT Aneka Tambang said on Tuesday it has told the government it was interested in taking part in the Busang gold find.

"We have written to mines and energy minister to ask to be involved in the Busang gold property. It is up to the government whether to agree to this," Aneka Tambang president director Darmoko Slamet told reporters.
"If the government agrees it will be good for the company, because Aneka Tambang has planned to go public if possible this year," he said.
He said the finance ministry has told the company should prepare to go public.
Aneka Tambang mines nickel in Sulawesi and gold in West Java.
"We have experienced in mining gold. We have the expertise. I don't think it will difficult to find fund if we are involve in Busang ," he said.
The company finance director Agus Umar Tochfa told Reuters the company assets had rised to 680 billion rupiah in 1996 from 634 billion rupiah in 1995.
"We know the government has said it will have a 10 percent stake in Busang. I think it would be good for Aneka Tambang to manage the government stake," Tochfa said.

Aneka Tambang said in statement it will produce 2.80 million tonnes of nickel ore in 1997, compared with 3.42 million tonnes in 1996. it planned to produce 10,200 tonnes ferronickel in 1997 against 9,553 tonnes in 1996.
The company will produce two tonnes of gold in 1997, compared with 1.8 tonnes in 1996.
A state control tin producer PT Tambang Timah had also expressed an interest in participating in Busang.
